# 01 Overview {background-color="#EF7C00"}

```{=html}
<div aria-labelledby="datasets-changelog-title" style="margin:1.2em auto 0;max-width:72%;padding:.55em .8em;border-left:3px solid #003D7C;border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;background:rgba(255,255,255,.78);color:#003D7C;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:.42em;line-height:1.35;">

  <ul style="margin:0;padding-left:1.2em;"><li><strong class="cp-text--navy">15 Sep 2026</strong> — Created the project-planning guide, expanded the catalogue to the full source inventory, and added a deck QR link.</li></ul>
```

## What this deck is for

- Find a **public, reproducible** dataset that makes a recommendation question possible.
- Match the data modality to the claim: ratings, sessions, text, social links, location, or impressions.
- Start small enough to establish classical and neural baselines before attempting a novel model.

::: {.callout-warning}
Dataset scale is not project quality. A well-scoped question, credible split, error analysis, and ethical critique matter more than a large download.
:::

::: notes
Delivery note: This is a project-planning resource, not a mandatory list. Ask teams to identify two candidates before committing. Sources: RecBole Dataset List; CP4285 project brief.
:::

## How to read a dataset slide

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Records</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Published count</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Interactions, impressions, or check-ins</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Footprint</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Download / RAM</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Published where available; otherwise an estimate</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Fit</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Task + risk</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">The research claim the data can support</span></div>
</div>
```

- **Published download** is the provider's compressed archive size when stated.
- **Planning RAM** is an indicative laptop/cluster budget for a parsed working subset; it varies with filtering, features, framework, and batch size.
- Every team must check the current licence, documentation, and terms before download.

::: notes
Delivery note: Make the distinction between file size and working memory explicit. Estimates are planning aids and should not be cited as provider specifications.
:::

# 02 Dataset Catalogue {background-color="#EF7C00"}

## Catalogue key

The catalogue is a **source inventory**, not a recommendation that every dataset is equally suitable or still equally accessible.

- **★** has a full project-planning slide in Section 03.
- Entries marked **textbook** were identified in the course books but are not separate RecBole entries.
- Dataset availability, licences, versions, and download sizes change; check the linked provider before building.

::: notes
Delivery note: Explain that the catalogue is intentionally broader than the detail section. The project-ready set is a curated subset, not the complete universe of available data.
:::

## Catalogue: shopping and transaction data I

| Dataset family / version | Primary signal | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon Reviews 2014 | Reviews + product metadata | 24 categories; 142.8M reviews |
| Amazon Reviews 2018 | Reviews + product metadata | 29 categories; 233.1M reviews |
| ★ Amazon Reviews 2023 | Reviews, metadata, images | 44 categories; 571.5M reviews |
| Amazon-M2 | Multilingual customer sessions | Six locales |
| Alibaba-iFashion | Outfit composition + item attributes | Fashion compatibility |

::: notes
Source: RecBole Dataset List, Shopping. Treat Amazon releases as distinct snapshots; choose one release and one category for a reproducible project.

# 03 Selected Dataset Details ⭐ {background-color="#EF7C00"}

## MovieLens 1M

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Interactions</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">1,000,209</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">6,040 users · 3,706 movies</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Footprint</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">6 MB ZIP</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Under 1 GB RAM for standard experiments</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Ratings</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">1-5 stars, timestamps, genres, demographics</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** transparent CF or ranking baselines; factorisation, neural CF, and genre-aware hybrids.

**Papers:** Harper & Konstan (2015), [*The MovieLens Datasets*](https://doi.org/10.1145/2827872){.paper-ref}; Koren, Bell & Volinsky (2009), [*Matrix Factorization Techniques for Recommender Systems*](https://doi.org/10.1109/MC.2009.263){.paper-ref}.

**URL:** <https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/1m/>

::: {.callout-warning}
The demographic fields are coarse and historic. Do not claim they represent contemporary audiences or use them casually as protected-attribute ground truth.
:::

::: notes
Sources: GroupLens, MovieLens 1M Dataset (1,000,209 ratings, 6 MB); Harper & Konstan, 2015, ACM TiiS; Koren et al., 2009, Computer. Source URL: https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/1m/
:::

## Amazon Reviews 2023 - select one category

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Catalogue scale</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">571.5M</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Reviews across 44 categories</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Footprint</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Varies</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Use one category + a documented k-core</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Hybrid</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Ratings, reviews, metadata, images by category</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** item cold start, review-aware recommendation, retrieval from product text, or an LLM-assisted explanation study.

**Papers:** McAuley et al. (2015), [*Image-based Recommendations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.04757){.paper-ref}; Hou et al. (2024), [*Amazon Reviews 2023*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03952){.paper-ref}.

**URL:** <https://amazon-reviews-2023.github.io/>

::: {.callout-warning}
Choose a category before downloading. Reviews are not neutral preference labels; helpfulness, popularity, and seller incentives can bias what is observed.
:::

::: notes
Sources: Amazon Reviews 2023 project; RecBole Dataset List; McAuley et al., 2015, SIGIR. The 571.54M / 44-category catalogue statistic is from RecBole. The source does not specify one uniform archive size because it depends on category and modalities.
:::

## Yelp Open Dataset

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Reviews</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">6.99M</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">150,346 businesses · 11 metro areas</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Footprint</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">~4.4 GB ZIP</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Plan 8-16 GB RAM for full JSON processing</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Reviews + POIs</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Text, stars, attributes, hours, check-ins</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** business/POI recommendation using text and metadata; city-level temporal split; exposure and representation analysis.

**Source / papers:** Yelp (2022), [*Yelp Open Dataset*](https://business.yelp.com/data/resources/open-dataset/){.paper-ref}; He et al. (2017), [*Neural Collaborative Filtering*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05031){.paper-ref} (a useful rating-ranking baseline).

**URL:** <https://business.yelp.com/data/resources/open-dataset/>

::: notes
Sources: Yelp Open Dataset documentation (Round 15 statistics); RecBole Dataset List. Planning RAM is an estimate for parsed full JSON, not a provider guarantee. Recommend one city or a reproducible business-category subset.
:::

## MIND-small

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Behaviour logs</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">230,117</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">94,057 users · 65,238 news articles</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Clicks</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">347,727</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Use provided train / dev divisions</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Impressions + text</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Title, abstract, category, entities, click history</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** candidate ranking, news encoders, sequential interests, and ranking metrics such as AUC, MRR, and nDCG.

**Papers:** Wu et al. (2020), [*MIND*](https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.331/){.paper-ref}; Wu et al. (2019), [*NAML: Neural News Recommendation with Attentive Multi-View Learning*](https://doi.org/10.24963/ijcai.2019/536){.paper-ref}.

**URL:** <https://msnews.github.io/>

::: {.callout-warning}
Non-clicked impressions are observed non-clicks, not certain dislikes. Discuss position/exposure bias, short news life cycles, and misinformation harms.
:::

::: notes
Sources: Wu et al., 2020, ACL; MIND official site. MIND-small statistics use the published 94,057-user / 65,238-news / 230,117-impression / 347,727-click table. Download size varies by train/dev package and optional entity embeddings; scope these explicitly.
:::

## Diginetica

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Sessions</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">204,789</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">993,483 click events</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Items</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">43,136</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Average session length: 4.85</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Search sessions</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Clicks, queries, product metadata, prices</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** next-item ranking on short anonymous sessions; compare item-kNN, GRU4Rec, and Transformer/attention models.

**Papers:** Kotsifakos et al. (2019), *Diginetica: A Dataset for Session-based Recommendation*; Hidasi et al. (2016), [*Session-based Recommendations with Recurrent Neural Networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06939){.paper-ref}.

**URL:** <https://competitions.codalab.org/competitions/11161>

::: notes
Sources: Ravanmehr & Mohamadrezaei, 2023, Table 3.3; RecBole Dataset List. The competition distribution/mirror determines archive size. Session length-one filtering must be documented if applied.
:::

## YOOCHOOSE / RecSys Challenge 2015

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Sessions</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">7.98M</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">31.71M click/buy events</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Items</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">37,486</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">182 days · mean length 3.97</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Sessions</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">E-commerce clickstream and purchase signal</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** an ambitious sequential project. Work on a chronologically defined subset before scaling.

**Papers:** Hidasi et al. (2016), [*Session-based Recommendations with RNNs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06939){.paper-ref}; Tan et al. (2016), [*Improved Recurrent Neural Networks for Session-based Recommendations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08117){.paper-ref}.

**URL:** <https://2015.recsyschallenge.com/challenge.html>

::: {.callout-warning}
This is a session dataset, not a long-term personalised-profile dataset. Avoid claims about stable user preference or demographic fairness that the data cannot support.
:::

::: notes
Sources: Ravanmehr & Mohamadrezaei, 2023, Table 3.3; RecBole Dataset List; Hidasi et al., ICLR 2016. Provider archive size is mirror-dependent. A 1/64 or 1/16 chronological subset is normally enough for a course project.
:::

## Retailrocket

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Events</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">2.76M</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">1.41M visitors · 235,061 items</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Footprint</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">~340 MB CSV</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Plan 2-4 GB RAM after parsing</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">Events</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">View, add-to-cart, transaction, timestamps</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** event-type-aware sequential recommendation; compare whether carts/purchases should be weighted differently from views.

**Papers:** Hidasi & Karatzoglou (2018), [*Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847){.paper-ref}; Quadrana, Cremonesi & Jannach (2017), *Sequence-Aware Recommender Systems*.

**URL:** <https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/retailrocket/ecommerce-dataset>

::: notes
Sources: Retailrocket E-commerce Dataset documentation; Ravanmehr & Mohamadrezaei, 2023, Table 3.2; Quadrana et al., 2017. The CSV and RAM numbers are planning estimates; exact Kaggle packaging can change. Treat hashed IDs as non-interpretable identifiers.
:::

## Adressa

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Sessions</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">982,210</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">2.65M click events in a 16-day processed version</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric"><span class="cp-metric__label">Items</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">13,820</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Short sessions: mean length 2.7</span></div>
  <div class="cp-metric cp-metric--orange"><span class="cp-metric__label">Data</span><strong class="cp-metric__value">News sessions</strong><span class="cp-metric__meta">Reading events, article metadata/content by release</span></div>
</div>

```

**Best fit:** short-horizon news recommendation and temporal evaluation; compare session-only and text-aware ranking.

**Papers:** Gulla et al. (2017), [*The Adressa Dataset for News Recommendation*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3109859.3109912){.paper-ref}; Karimi et al. (2018), *News Recommender Systems*.

**URL:** <https://reclab.idi.ntnu.no/dataset/>

::: {.callout-warning}
News preference is volatile and politically consequential. Preserve time order, avoid leaking future article metadata, and analyse publisher/topic concentration.
:::

::: notes
Sources: Ravanmehr & Mohamadrezaei, 2023, Tables 3.2-3.3. Published counts are for a processed 16-day version, not every raw release. Check access terms and supplied article fields before choosing a modelling claim.
:::

```{=html}
</div>

```

**Best fit:** trust propagation, social regularisation, robustness, and cold-start comparison against a rating-only baseline.

**Papers:** Massa & Avesani (2006), *Trust-aware Recommender Systems*; Guo, Zhang & Yorke-Smith (2015), *TrustSVD*.

**URL:** <https://www.cse.msu.edu/~tangjili/trust.html>

::: {.callout-warning}
Trust links are neither ground-truth expertise nor similarity. The data are historical, so frame claims as benchmark evidence rather than contemporary behaviour.
:::

::: notes
Sources: Epinions trust dataset documentation; Massa & Avesani, 2006; Guo et al., 2015. Counts are the commonly used Epinions subset. Obtain the distribution only from its documented source and record the chosen version.
:::

## Choose a dataset by the claim you can defend

```{=html}
<div class="cp-grid cp-grid--3">
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--soft"><p class="cp-card__title">1. Define the task</p><p>Who receives what recommendation, from which signal, at what time?</p></div>
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--soft"><p class="cp-card__title">2. Lock the split</p><p>Use a chronological split for sequential, news, or context-sensitive claims.</p></div>
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--soft"><p class="cp-card__title">3. Establish baselines</p><p>Start with popularity and a classical model before a neural/LLM system.</p></div>
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--soft"><p class="cp-card__title">4. Evaluate the interface</p><p>Use ranking metrics for top-k recommendation; inspect coverage and diversity too.</p></div>
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--soft"><p class="cp-card__title">5. Analyse failure</p><p>Segment by activity level, item popularity, time, and relevant content groups.</p></div>
  <div class="cp-card cp-card--warning"><p class="cp-card__title">6. Address people</p><p>Document licence, provenance, privacy, exposure, representation, and likely harms.</p></div>
</div>
```

::: notes
Delivery note: The same implementation can make a weak or strong project depending on its formulation and evaluation. Tie this slide to the project rubric.
:::

## A reproducibility checklist

- Record the exact source URL, download date, licence/terms, version, and checksum where supplied.
- Define every filter: event types retained, k-core threshold, sessionisation rule, and minimum sequence length.
- Split before fitting any data-dependent representation; do not let future interactions or item text leak into training.
- Publish a configuration for popularity, ItemKNN/BPR/MF, and the advanced model on the same split.
- Report resource use: sampled records, download size, GPU/CPU, RAM, training time, and random seeds.
- Separate an observed non-click from a negative preference unless the task design justifies the assumption.

::: notes
Delivery note: Ask teams to bring these six fields to the Week 7 project critique. Source: CP4285 project brief; RecBole data-format documentation.
:::
